question: What is the structure of Uganda's agricultural sector and is commercial farming exempt from tax?
answer: Uganda's agricultural sector employs approximately 68% of the working population, accounts for 24% of national GDP, 35% of export earnings, and supports 7 million farming households (80% of all households). While 80% of Uganda's land is arable, only 35% is currently under cultivation. There is a common misconception that farming is tax-exempt; this is NOT true. Under Section 35 of the Income Tax Act, commercial farmers are recognized as business income earners: gross farm receipts are taxable, and legitimate farming operational expenditures (seeds, agrochemicals, veterinary services, casual labor, and repairs) are allowable deductions when computing chargeable income.

question: What tax incentives and deductions are available for agribusiness startups and employers of persons with disabilities?
answer: Under the URA Agricultural Taxation Guide (Vol. 1 Issue 4 FY 2025-26): 1) Citizen Startup Income Tax Holiday (effective 1 July 2025): Any startup agribusiness established by a Ugandan citizen with an investment capital not exceeding UGX 500 million is 100% exempt from income tax for three (3) consecutive years, provided the citizen/associate has not previously benefited from the exemption and files annual returns; 2) Employment of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs): Private agricultural employers who prove that at least 5% of their full-time workforce are persons with disabilities are entitled to an indefinite deduction of 2% of income tax payable; 3) 6% WHT Exemption: All agricultural supplies are statutorily exempt from 6% Withholding Tax indefinitely, and compliant agribusinesses can obtain a 12-month renewable WHT exemption certificate on other supplies and professional fees.

question: What are the specific tax rules and capital deductions for floriculture and greenhouse farming in Uganda?
answer: Under URA floriculture guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/floriculture-farming-and-export/ and the Agriculture Sector Guide: 1) Uganda's floriculture sector is a top 10 foreign exchange earner (~$30 million annually), exporting 98% of flower production to the Netherlands (90% via Dutch flower auctions, 10% direct to florists), primarily roses and cuttings; 2) Commercial flower exports are zero-rated (0% VAT) under Schedule 3 of the VAT Act; 3) Greenhouse & Plant Capital Deduction: Under the Income Tax Act, capital expenditure incurred on the acquisition or establishment of a horticultural plant or construction of a greenhouse (including land clearing and drainage costs) is allowed as an accelerated straight-line capital deduction of 20% per year across five (5) consecutive years (100% total write-off).

question: What tax exemptions and customs incentives apply to poultry farming in Uganda?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/poultry-faming/: 1) Poultry Breeders & Parent Stock: Under the Fifth Schedule of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), broiler and layer parent stock imported for raising breeder flocks that produce hatching eggs are 100% exempt from all customs duties and taxes for poultry farmers (VAT exempt when imported by dealers); hatching eggs are strictly for producing day-old chicks and never for retail food consumption; 2) Equipment & Inputs: Incubators, hatcheries, day-old chicks, poultry feeds, and veterinary acaricides/drugs are exempt from all import taxes under EACCMA Fifth Schedule Part B; 3) Feeds: Under the VAT Act, animal and poultry feeds, along with raw mixed components (feed additives, eggshells, wheat bran, maize bran, seed cake, concentrates, premixes) are VAT-exempt supplies.

question: What VAT and customs exemptions apply to agri-input dealers and agricultural machinery?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/agri-input-dealers/ and EACCMA Fifth Schedule Part B: 1) Agricultural Machinery & Implements: Agricultural tractors, hoes, ploughs, harrows, seeders, planters, transplanters, manure spreaders, fertilizer distributors, agricultural sprayers, refrigerated trucks, and aluminum dairy cans are exempt from all customs duties and taxes when imported by agriculturalists, and VAT exempt when imported by input dealers; 2) Inputs: Fertilizers, seeds for sowing, fungicides, and pesticides are exempt from all taxes under EACCMA upon MAAIF approval and zero-rated (0% VAT) under the VAT Act; 3) Irrigation Works: Sprinklers, irrigation works, and ready-to-use drip lines are 100% tax exempt under EACCMA for farmers and VAT exempt for dealers.

question: What taxes and export incentives apply to agro-processing industries in Uganda?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/agro-processing-industry-al/: 1) Agro-processing entails adding industrial value to raw agricultural products (dairy processing, grain milling, peanut paste 'odii', sugar, fruit processing, meat/fish packaging, animal feeds); 2) Standard domestic taxes apply: 30% Corporation Tax on net chargeable profits, PAYE on employees, and 18% VAT; 3) 10-Year Income Tax Holiday: Under Section 21(1)(y) of the Income Tax Act, agro-processors who invest in industrial parks or free zones and export at least 80% of their production outside the domestic tariff area enjoy a 10-year income tax holiday; 4) Machinery: Dairy processing machinery enjoys 0% import duty under the EAC Common External Tariff (CET) and VAT exemption; 5) Digital Tax Stamps (DTS): Processed gazetted beverages (packaged water, juices, alcoholic drinks, sugar) must bear Digital Tax Stamps.

question: Where can I download the official URA Guide to Taxation of the Agricultural Sector?
answer: The official booklet 'A GUIDE TO TAXATION OF THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR' (Vol. 1 Issue 4 FY 2025-2026, 28 pages) is downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2026/01/A-GUIDE-TO-TAXATION-OF-THE-AGRICULTURAL-SECTOR-VOL-1-ISSUE-4-FY-2025-2026.pdf and cross-referenced under URA Tax Education across Agribusiness (https://ura.go.ug/en/category/tax-education/agriculture/agribusiness/ and /test/), Crop Farming (/crop-farming/), Poultry (/poultry-faming/), Floriculture (/floriculture-farming-and-export/), Agri-Inputs (/agri-input-dealers/), and Agro-Processing (/agro-processing-industry-al/).
